title: Add entropy-aware canary stabilizer and traffic-weighted fallback guard
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Adds an entropy-based stabilizer to reduce false-positive canary flips during bursty traffic and a traffic-weighted fallback guard that biases rollouts toward stable traffic slices. Improves canary resilience and reduces unnecessary rollbacks.
description:
Context and motivation: Some canary runs were flip-flopping under short-lived traffic bursts and non-uniform traffic slices; P50 remained steady but tail jitter and metric heterogeneity caused noisy detectors to trigger rollbacks. This PR implements an entropy-aware stabilizer that measures distributional uncertainty across latency/throughput fingerprints and an orthogonal traffic-weighted fallback guard that reduces the influence of small or noisy traffic slices on rollout decisions.

Design summary: The stabilizer computes a per-route entropy score over a rolling histogram of latency percentiles and request fingerprints; high entropy indicates multimodal or bursty behavior and triggers adaptive threshold widening for a configurable cooldown window. The fallback guard assigns per-slice weights by a traffic significance estimator (combining qps, user segments, and model variant exposure) and modifies canary scoring so that low-weight slices cannot single-handedly flip the global canary state. Both components are pluggable detectors in the canary orchestration pipeline and configurable via perf-canary config (defaults tuned for web-search and conversational workloads).

What changed (high level):
- New stabilizer implementation: canary/entropy_stabilizer.py (core logic), canary/entropy_metrics.go (runtime metrics + exporter)
- Traffic-weighted fallback guard: canary/traffic_weights.rs (estimator + integration)
- Orchestration integration: canary/orchestrator_controller.go (hook points, feature flag)
- Config + defaults: charts/perf-canary/values.yaml, docs/perf-canary/entropy-stabilizer.md
- Tests and harness: integration_tests/canary_entropy_integration_test.py, load_tests/entropy_shard_simulator.py
- Minor: updated telemetry schemas and added dashboard template: observability/dashboards/canary_entropy.json

Commits (summary):
- Add entropy-based stabilizer core (Maya Patel)
- Add traffic-weighted fallback estimator and integration (Maya Patel)
- Hook stabilizer into orchestrator and feature flag (Maya Patel)
- Add unit and integration tests + load harness (Maya Patel)
- Docs and chart defaults (Maya Patel)
- Fix flakey timing in integration test and add retries (Maya Patel)

Testing and results: Unit tests cover histogram aggregation and entropy thresholds; integration tests run a 30m synthetic canary with three traffic slices and validate that under bursty input the stabilizer prevents a premature rollback in 9/10 simulated runs. Load harness shows a 40% reduction in rollbacks for generated bursty traces while maintaining detection of real regressions in injected-failure experiments. Telemetry added to track stabilizer triggers, entropy score distribution, and slice weights.

Rollout plan: Feature-gated behind perf_feature.entropy_stabilizer. Phased rollout: (1) enable in staging for 2 weeks with debug telemetry; (2) enable for 10% of canary traffic in prod for 1 week; (3) increase to 50% and monitor with alarm on unexpected rollback drop or missed-regressions. A kill-switch is provided to disable the stabilizer if necessary.

Backward compatibility and config: Default behavior is opt-in (feature flag false) and safe defaults that only widen thresholds, not skip regressions. Config fields documented in charts/perf-canary/values.yaml. No breaking changes to canary API.

CI and reliability notes: Initial CI run showed a flaky integration test due to timing; I added retries and a small test harness sleep to stabilize. After rerun, all checks passed. Performance regression tests included a targeted P90/P99 injection matrix.

Related work: This complements earlier canary detectors by adding distributional awareness; links to ENG-8342 (canary noise reduction initiative) and SRE-120 (incident follow-up from PROD-2025-09).

Request: Reviewers — would like particular attention on the traffic-weighted estimator math (canary/traffic_weights.rs) and the threshold tuning chosen for conversational workloads.

Merge notes: Squash-merged after approvals and CI pass.
